Yes—almost certainly.

At **9.1° altitude**, the Moon is above the **east-southeastern horizon** (azimuth **109°**) and should be readily visible if buildings, hills, or trees do not block that direction. It is **91% illuminated**, so it will be very bright, and the Sun is already **16° below the horizon**, making the sky quite dark despite the remaining astronomical twilight.

Look roughly **one fist-width above the horizon at arm’s length**, a little south of due east. Atmospheric haze and extinction will dim and redden it somewhat at that low altitude, but under the stated clear conditions, an ordinary observer should have no difficulty spotting it. The main uncertainty is simply whether your local horizon is unobstructed.
